findings.evidence: `find crates -name mod.rs` returns crates/oqueue-broker/src/fetch/mod.rs and produce/mod.rs (both added by bbd1f65, M3.14), join_group/mod.rs (99afbea, M4.7) and join_group/round/mod.rs (6972503, M4.15d). Every other M4 handler follows the convention rule 8 states -- find_coordinator.rs beside find_coordinator/, sync_group.rs beside sync_group/, heartbeat.rs beside heartbeat/, leave_group.rs, offset_commit.rs, offset_fetch.rs -- so join_group is the one M4 module that does not. Compare docs/internal/standards/code-structure.md:17 ("Each rule names its gate, or is marked as having none"), rule 8 at :58, and the "What has no gate" section at :131-139, which names only two things and not rule 8; `grep -rn 'mod\.rs' scripts/` finds no gate, only scripts/gates/m4-complete.sh:160, which hardcodes `join_group/mod.rs` in its handler list and therefore encodes the violation. reviews/milestone-M1-4920f1685c9fde40.json finding f360cf459329 raised the identical rule at `minor` with an empty task_id when the tree held one instance; nothing was scheduled, and the count is now four. Graded minor for consistency with that precedent and with review.md rule 9 -- it changes no behaviour -- but it is the second milestone review to find it, so it belongs in a sweep row for whichever milestone opens next rather than in a fifth M4 round.
findings.summary: code-structure.md rule 8 ("No mod.rs") has four violations in the tree, two of them added by M4, and the standard's own "What has no gate" section does not list the rule -- so a rule that names no gate reads as if it has one.
